abstract: OpenAI's preprint, whose main theorem states that $\zeta(s)\ne0$ for $\Re s>7/8$, and Liu's improvements work with residue symbols over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. One input is a second-moment bound for Möbius-weighted sums of residue symbols, proved through Patterson's cubic theta function. We study the quartic analogue over $\mathbb Q(i)$, where no such theta description is available. For primary squarefree $c$ with split prime factors, the normalised quartic Gauss sum satisfies $\gamma_1(c)^2=\mu(c)\,(c/|c|)\,\chi_c(-1)$, a form of the classical square formula, so it carries the Möbius function in its square. A row twist carries $\mu$ in this way only in one orientation, where the rows are Gauss sums at cube numerators; there the quartic theta residue vanishes on all but the $\asymp X^{1/2}$ rows with squarefull odd part. We prove that the mean square of the carrier sums over rows of norm about $X$ is $\ll X^{2+\theta+\varepsilon}$ whenever twisted quartic Möbius large sieves have excess $B^{\theta}$ uniformly in twists of conductor up to $X^{1/2-2\theta}$ and in coprimality conditions of norm up to $2X$. Without the last restriction the hypothesis is false. The largest shortfall occurs where rows and columns have norm about $X$, and there the Möbius sieve is the Poisson dual of the carrier energy. De Faveri's quartic large sieve gives $X^{9/4+\varepsilon}$, and GRH gives $X^{2+\varepsilon}$; heuristically, for rows and columns of equal norm and with pointwise control of $1/L$, a zero-density estimate with exponent $\kappa$ gives excess $\max(0,1-2/\kappa)$. In a transcription of Liu's optimisation, labelled a model, every admissible point has exponent at least $9/10$ for the generic excess $1/4$, and beating Liu's $0.87446830769$ needs $\theta<0.18617$; the energy-based Cauchy–Schwarz estimate does not establish the model's direct-side assumption for the one complete quartic observation known. Up to $X=2^{15}$ the carrier energy is within $6\%$ of the random-phase expectation. No zero-free region is proved.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary: Two paragraphs added to Section 5 and two sentences to Section 1, item 5; all numbers, Theorem 3.1 and its proof are unchanged. The new paragraph "Which constraint binds" states that in the quartic model the length bound l <= 1/5 is the only binding constraint: replacing it by l <= lmax gives B = 1 - lmax/2 with the Poisson side slack, up to Liu's 1 - 3l > 0 (B = 5/6). It explains the role of l < 1/5 in Liu's cubic direct estimate with free total length: at M = N the reflection term (5l-1)_+/4 of his excess k(M,l) vanishes exactly for l <= 1/5, and in the cubic case the bound does not bind (full k, free M, no bound on l returns 0.8749570302 at l = 0.1668). The quartic model has no quartic reflection term, and adding the cubic ones does not restore the bound. So the threshold 0.18617 assumes Liu's cubic range; this is now said in Section 5 and item 5. The second new paragraph, "Saving in the Gram-type term", adds the exact model bound (5.5): if a fraction s of the exponent of the term z b/2 (the analogue of the exceptional-frequency term in the Gram bound of [1, Proposition 15.2]) were saved, B >= 0.9 - g/2 - (s/8)(9/20 - 3g/2), attained at l = 1/5, M = 2N - 4g. At theta = 1/4 any s > 0.4539 beats B*, with caveats (optimum at M = 2N, the validity condition may change, (T2) unproved; in the cubic case the term is a positive mean term by [1, (13.8)], so a saving needs a different row polynomial). New supplement scripts cubic_fullk.py, quartic_fe.py, iso_l.py, gram_s.py with logs.
title: Quartic Gauss sums with a Möbius carrier, and the large-sieve input a quartic version of the 7/8 method would need
